newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-FORGIVING HOLYFIELD SAYS SPORT WILL BENEFIT IN LONG RUN.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-FORGIVING HOLYFIELD SAYS SPORT WILL BENEFIT IN LONG RUN.

text.p: Heavyweight champion Evander Holyfield was in a forgiving mood on Tuesday and said Mike Tyson's vicious biting of his ears in their title fight could be good for boxing in the long run, if the punishment sends the right message.

"What has been done has been done. I thank the Lord that I don't have permament injury," the classy three-time heavyweight champion said on CNN's Larry King Live, one of several television interviews Holyfield gave from his Fairburn, Georgia home Tuesday.

"The little piece of ear that's gone is not really important and you just hope that he's learned from what he's done," added Holyfield, who said he would not bring charges against Tyson, who was disqualified from their fight Saturday after twice biting Holyfield's ears in the third round.
Holyfield said after the first bite, during the break while a decision was being made as to whether to continue the fight, he had prayed, trying to get his focus back.
Because, he admitted, "at first I wanted to go in and bite him back."

The Nevada State Athletic Commission earlier Tuesday moved to keep Tyson under suspension pending a disciplinary hearing next week, after which it will decide whether to ban Tyson from boxing, and for how long, as well as determine a possible fine.
Holyfield said if the commission does the right thing in handing down a severe enough penalty, then the injuries he suffered would have served a positive purpose.
"I think what happend is going to shape the game of boxing and make it better," he predicted on MSNBC's InterNight programme.
He said a stiff penalty could change the attitude of many boxers.

"I don't think (the ear biting) hurt the sport as much as helped," Holyfield said. "I think that boxing needed an eye opener for the commisioners and the referees and the judges to see how we can better the game of boxing for the up and coming fighters."
He said the Nevada officials have a chance to make a decision that will, "make all the fighters never, ever want to do anything like that.
"...let's get the whole game of boxing to make a pitch to be better," he pleaded.
Asked if he thought Tyson's suspension should be at least two years, he said, "yeah, that or more because you (only) fight once or twice a year usually."
The 34-year-old champ said he would be willing to talk to Tyson.

"I don't hold grudges or anything. What has happened has happened and it's time to move on to a positive situation to how we can prevent this from happening to any other boxer," added Holyfield, who said he expects to fight again in November against a yet to be determined opponent.
While Holyfield accepted the apology Tyson offered at a news conference Monday, he said only time will tell if it was sincere.
"If time proves that he's able to conduct himself in the proper way then it's obviously the truth," Holyfield said.
But Holyfield took exception to Tyson's repeated accustions that the champion had intentionally head butted him during the fight, which Tyson claims made him "snap."

"I never ever intentionally head butted anybody because I know you can really injure somebody," Holyfield said. "If you watch the tape you can see it's not a head but. I hit him with a left hook and cut him."
Holyfield said it was frustration that led to the biting incident.
He said after losing to Holyfield last November, Tyson came back believing "he was more than ready this time" but "in this fight, the same thing was happening and I think the frustration got to him."
But Holyfield was definitely not buying the Tyson just snapped excuse.
"The second time you knew it was intentional. When you snap you don't repeatedly do it," added Holyfield, who said he is scheduled to get the stitches removed from his mangled ear on Wednesday.
In yet another interview, with NBC, Holyfield actually said he could envision getting back into the ring with Tyson somewhere down the road.
"After he comes off suspension, and he fights the proper fights, and if it's something that people want to see, then I would more than welcome it."
